messages.subject: Confusing regarding inla.group.cv
parts:
Hi,

I have run into some confusion regarding the inla.group.cv function. In my understanding a cross validation prediction should only depend on the data from other folds, but it seems the predictions in cv$mean are affected by the data in its own fold. This is clear from one of the groups be a large outlier. I hope it is clear what I mean from the plots in the below toy example. Have I misunderstood what the function is supposed to do, or did I maybe misspecify the groups (I followed the vignette)?

n = 50
grp.len = 5
x = rnorm(n)
g = rnorm(grp.len)

g[1] = 200 # Outlier to detect "cheating"

grp = rep(1:grp.len, each = n %/% grp.len)
y = 1 + x + g[grp] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.01)

dat = data.frame(y, x, grp)

df_grp = as.data.frame(matrix(rep(NA, ncol(dat) * grp.len),
                              ncol = ncol(dat)))
colnames(df_grp) <- colnames(dat)
df_grp$grp = 1:grp.len

dat_ext = rbind(dat, df_grp)

r = inla(y ~ x + f(grp, model = "iid"),
         data = dat_ext,
         control.compute = list(config=TRUE))

groups <- lapply(1:(dim(dat_ext)[1]),
                 function(i) which(dat_ext$grp == dat_ext$grp[i]))

cv <- inla.group.cv(r, groups = groups)

# Proof of cheating:
#plot(r$summary.fitted.values$mean[1:50]) # "allowed" cheating
#plot(r$summary.fitted.values$mean[51:55]) # "allowed" cheating
#plot(r$summary.random$grp$mean) # "allowed" cheating
plot(cv$mean[1:50]) # Cheating
plot(cv$mean[51:55]) # Cheating

messages.author: 83ef5784934df8fd
messages.subject: Re: Confusing regarding inla.group.cv
parts: And a further question: is the trick I did by extending dat to dat_ext a reasonable way to get cv-predictions for the levels of grp? I.e., a part of the latent field?

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Confusing regarding inla.group.cv
parts:
I have discussed this case with Zhedong (cc'ed above), and it seems that
the impact of '200' is simply to large to be able to compute the cv with
'adjusting' the joint estimate. in particular, the changes '200' have on
the hyperparameters is the main driver, and if you fix the
hyperparmeters and rerun the examples, then you're results will look way
better.

the current computations of the cv or group.cv, all assumes that we can
correct the joint estimate to get the estimate when y[i] is removed
(this also includes the hyperparaemters). this implicitely assumes that
the posterior |y and |y[-i] are not to far away, which is not the case
in your example.

Best
Havard
